data.narrative:
Monumental is a Series B robotics and manufacturing company founded by Salar al Khafaji and Sebastiaan Visser that has raised $32M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of 9 comparable companies—1 public and 8 private—including same-stage robotics firms Generalist AI, Bedrock Robotics, and Dexterity.

Two triangulation methods were applied. The stage-progression method uses the $32M total raised as a proxy base value and applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement, yielding $61M. The peer-median method benchmarks against three same-sector, same-stage comparables with a median valuation of $1.8B and a range from $1.6B to $2.0B. This wide peer range reflects significant heterogeneity in the robotics sector even within the Series B cohort.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $52M to $2.0B, with a median triangulation of $905M. The substantial dispersion between stage-progression ($61M) and peer-median ($1.8B) reflects genuine uncertainty about whether Monumental's market opportunity and competitive position align with sector-leading peers or represent an earlier-stage risk profile. Key uncertainties include customer traction relative to the peer set, technology differentiation in a crowded frontier-robotics landscape, and whether comparable companies command premium valuations justified by defensibility or market timing. Further diligence on revenue, unit economics, and customer concentration is required to narrow this range.
